title: The simple prepositions
description: a, di, da, in, con, su, per, tra/fra — for place, movement, time and possession.
objectives: Know the core meanings of the nine simple prepositions.
Express place and movement (a, in, da).
Express time (in, a, per, tra, da) and possession (di).

blocks.caption: Core meanings
rows: of; possession; origin with essere; material
il libro di Marco; sono di Roma
to, at; cities; time of day; + infinitive after some verbs
vado a Roma; a mezzanotte; comincio a leggere
vengo da Milano; vado dal nonno; studio da tre mesi
in, into; countries, regions; means of transport; seasons
in Italia; in giardino; in treno; in estate
sul tavolo; un libro sugli animali
for; through; in order to; duration
per te; per due ore; studio per imparare

blocks.title: Prepositions do not map one-to-one
blocks.text: No Italian preposition has a single English equivalent, and fixed expressions are common (*a casa, a scuola, a letto, in montagna, in vacanza, al mare*). Learn prepositions in phrases rather than as single words.

blocks.title: No difference between 'in' and 'to'
blocks.text: Italian uses the same preposition for being somewhere and going there: *Sono a Roma / Vado a Roma*; *Sono in giardino / Vado in giardino*.

blocks.title: da + person
blocks.text: *da* + a person or a shop means 'at/to someone's place': *Sono dalla nonna* (I'm at Grandma's), *Vado dal medico* (I'm going to the doctor's).

items: *in* + season or month: *in estate, in inverno, in dicembre*.
*a* + hour, festival: *a mezzogiorno, alle tre, a Natale*.
*tra / fra* + amount of time = in … from now: *tra un'ora* (in an hour).
*da* + amount of time with the present = for/since (still continuing): *Abito qui da due anni* (I have lived here for two years).

examples.it: Il cane di Sara è nero.
Vado a scuola con mio fratello.
examples.en: I go to school with my brother.
In summer we go to the seaside.

exercises.prompt: Complete with di, da, con or per.
exercises.text: Il libro {0} Marco è sul tavolo. Vengo {1} Torino. Gioco {2} il gatto. Questo regalo è {3} te.
exercises.explanation: di = possession; da = origin; con = with; per = for.
tra/fra + time = in … from now. per un'ora would mean 'for an hour'.

mistakes.message: per un'ora = for (the duration of) an hour. 'In an hour from now' is fra (or tra) un'ora.

exercises.answer: Il cane di Sara è nero.
exercises.explanation: Italian has no 's: il cane di Sara.

exercises.answer: I have lived here for two years.
accept: I've lived here for two years
I have been living here for two years
I've been living here for two years
exercises.explanation: da + time with the present tense = an action that started in the past and continues.

summary: di (of, possession), a (to/at, cities), da (from, someone's place, since), in (in/into, countries), con (with), su (on), per (for), tra/fra (between, in … time).
The same preposition expresses position and movement: sono a Roma / vado a Roma.
da + present for ongoing duration: abito qui da due anni.

title: Articulated prepositions
description: di, a, da, in, su combined with the definite article: del, al, dal, nel, sul…
objectives: Form all articulated prepositions from the table.
Recognise them in reading: nel bosco, sulla spiaggia, dalla nonna.

blocks.text: When *di, a, da, in, su* are followed by a definite article, they merge with it into one word. *in* becomes *ne-* and *di* becomes *de-*.

blocks.title: Building the form
blocks.text: Take the article and attach it: *a + il = al*; with an article beginning with l, double the l: *a + la = alla*, *a + lo = allo*, *a + l' = all'*.

blocks.title: con, per, tra, fra do not contract
blocks.text: Modern Italian writes *con il, con la, per il, tra i*. (The forms *col* and *coi* exist but are optional and informal.)

items: Place: *nel bosco, sulla spiaggia, nella tana, sull'albero*.
Movement: *al mare, alla finestra, dal nonno*.
Possession with a noun that takes the article: *la casa della nonna, il nido dell'uccello*.
Time: *alle tre* (at three o'clock), *dalle otto* (from eight o'clock).

blocks.title: No article, no contraction
blocks.text: Where the noun normally has no article, the simple preposition stays: *a Roma, di Marco, in Italia, a casa, a scuola*. Compare *in giardino* (fixed phrase) and *nel giardino della nonna* (a specific garden).

examples.en: The fox goes back into its den.
The squirrel is in the tree.

examples.it: Il nido dell'uccello è sul ramo.
examples.en: The bird's nest is on the branch.

examples.it: Compro del pane e delle mele.
examples.en: I'm buying some bread and some apples.

exercises.explanation: in becomes ne-: ne + l = nel.

exercises.prompt: Write the contraction of *di* with each article.
exercises.explanation: di → de- + article; l doubled before articles beginning with l.
alberi takes gli: su + gli = sugli.
City names take no article, so no contraction: a Roma.

exercises.text: La casa {0} (di + la) nonna è vicino {1} (a + il) fiume. Andiamo {2} (da + i) cugini.

exercises.prompt: Translate: The fox goes back into its den.
accept: La volpe torna nella sua tana.
exercises.explanation: in + la = nella. Italian often omits the possessive when ownership is obvious.

summary: di, a, da, in, su + article merge: del, al, dal, nel, sul; della, alla, dalla, nella, sulla…
Double l before articles beginning with l (alla, dello, nell').
No article (a Roma, di Marco, a casa) → no contraction.
con, per, tra, fra are written separately.
